title: High-Performance Database-Adjacent Substrate Audit v1
principle: PostgreSQL is the enterprise operational substrate. JSON/JSONL/CSV remain the portable, inspectable, replayable, schema-governed source-of-truth/evidence layer. DuckDB remains a disposable analytical/read-side substrate. SQLite remains forbidden. High-performance adjacent tooling may strengthen ingestion, projection, replay, analytics, cockpit UX, static docs, procurement evidence packs, context retrieval, and enterprise debuggability — but never at the expense of artifact-first doctrine or PostgreSQL operational authority.

current_substrate_inventory.current_role: In-memory DuckDB analytics engine — ingests JSONL files via read_json_auto, executes SQL views for cockpit widgets
current_substrate_inventory.performance_constraints: Full JSONL reparse on every engine init. No incremental refresh. In-memory — data lost on process restart.
current_substrate_inventory.bottleneck_evidence: read_json_auto reparses every JSONL file on every AnalyticsEngine initialization. No caching. All widget queries execute fresh SQL aggregations — no materialized view equivalent.
current_substrate_inventory.adjacent_tool_potential: DuckDB already dominates this need well. Parquet snapshots could seed cold-start without full JSONL reparse. Arrow batches could feed cockpit projections without dict-of-dicts overhead.

current_substrate_inventory.current_role: Filesystem-backed canonical receipt envelope store — JSON envelope files + manifest.jsonl index
current_substrate_inventory.performance_constraints: _list_from_manifest() does full manifest.jsonl linear scan, in-memory reversal, then N individual get() calls (file read + JSON parse + Pydantic validate per envelope). _manifest_line_count() reads entire file byte-by-byte.
current_substrate_inventory.bottleneck_evidence: O(N) manifest scan + N*O(1) file reads per list() call. No caching. Repeated list() calls redo identical work.
current_substrate_inventory.adjacent_tool_potential: DuckDB-backed manifest index would eliminate linear scan. Postgres receipt_envelope table (post-migration) makes list() a single indexed query.

current_substrate_inventory.performance_constraints: find_existing_report() does linear scan of entire JSONL ledger with JSON parse per line. No index by dedupe_key.
current_substrate_inventory.bottleneck_evidence: O(N) scan per dedupe_key lookup. Append-only write is fine — JSONL append is correct for canonical ledgers.
current_substrate_inventory.adjacent_tool_potential: Postgres finding table (post-migration) enables O(1) dedupe_key lookup. DuckDB on reports JSONL already provides analytical views.

current_substrate_inventory.current_role: Event fabric JSONL append + read — content-light event stream with redaction enforcement
current_substrate_inventory.performance_constraints: f.flush() on every append — sync I/O per event. read() returns entire file in memory. _validate_event() recursively walks nested payload checking 50-field blocklist.
current_substrate_inventory.bottleneck_evidence: Sync flush per event write. Full-file reads. Recursive redaction scan per event (O(keys*depth*50)).
current_substrate_inventory.adjacent_tool_potential: Batch append with periodic flush would reduce sync I/O. DuckDB projections already exist for event fabric reads (rig_relay/events/duckdb_projection.py). Postgres event_log table (post-migration) eliminates file-based read bottlenecks entirely.

current_substrate_inventory.current_role: File-backed coordination store — sessions, tasks, leases, artifacts, conflicts. fcntl digester lock for cross-process safety.
current_substrate_inventory.source_of_truth_status: dual authority — events.jsonl is canonical; file state is operational
current_substrate_inventory.performance_constraints: fcntl.LOCK_EX serializes all coordination event writes. events.jsonl grows unbounded — no compaction. _next_sequence() scans entire events.jsonl to find max sequence.
current_substrate_inventory.bottleneck_evidence: Single-writer bottleneck under fcntl. Unbounded events.jsonl growth makes sequence derivation O(N) over time.
current_substrate_inventory.adjacent_tool_potential: Postgres advisory locks (pg_advisory_lock) replace fcntl for cross-process coordination. Postgres coordination_lease table (post-migration) eliminates event.jsonl scan for sequence numbers.

current_substrate_inventory.current_role: Cockpit projection assembly — reads multiple JSON artifacts from .build/rig-relay/, assembles content-light projection dict
current_substrate_inventory.source_of_truth_status: runtime-only computed state — rebuildable from artifacts
current_substrate_inventory.performance_constraints: Full read of all source artifacts on every projection refresh. No caching. No incremental reload.
current_substrate_inventory.bottleneck_evidence: I/O-bound on number of source files. _load_json() swallows all exceptions — masks corruption.
current_substrate_inventory.adjacent_tool_potential: Postgres materialized views (post-migration) replace projection assembly. LISTEN/NOTIFY provides incremental invalidation. Arrow batches could reduce dict-of-dicts overhead in projection payload.

current_substrate_inventory.current_role: Content-light enforcement — recursive dict walk with regex matching against forbidden field patterns
current_substrate_inventory.source_of_truth_status: content-light enforcement boundary — applied before artifact write
current_substrate_inventory.performance_constraints: 5 pre-compiled regex patterns + 50-field frozenset checked recursively against every nested key. O(keys*depth*patterns).
current_substrate_inventory.bottleneck_evidence: Per-event redaction is the gatekeeper before any artifact write. Should remain vigilant — optimization through caching of known-safe schema fields is acceptable but must not weaken enforcement.
current_substrate_inventory.adjacent_tool_potential: pg_jsonschema or CHECK constraints (post-migration) provide second-layer enforcement at database boundary. Content-light enforcement must still happen at application layer as primary defense.

current_substrate_inventory.current_role: Static documentation site renderer — reads docs/json/*.json, renders to HTML/CSS/JS, produces search index
current_substrate_inventory.source_of_truth_status: derived artifact — docs/json/*.json are canonical; rendered HTML is generated
current_substrate_inventory.performance_constraints: Loads all JSON files into memory simultaneously. I/O-bound on file count. No incremental rendering.
current_substrate_inventory.bottleneck_evidence: ~200 JSON files currently — acceptable. Would be problematic at 10k+ pages.
current_substrate_inventory.adjacent_tool_potential: Parquet snapshot of schema registry could seed the search index without re-reading all JSON files. Arrow batches could accelerate page rendering.

current_substrate_inventory.current_role: JSONL-to-Parquet compaction via DuckDB read_json_auto + COPY FORMAT PARQUET
current_substrate_inventory.source_of_truth_status: derived artifact — JSONL files are canonical; Parquet is analytical snapshot
current_substrate_inventory.performance_constraints: read_json_auto reparses full JSONL files. COPY FORMAT PARQUET is efficient for write. No Parquet read-back in production path — only in rollup queries.
current_substrate_inventory.bottleneck_evidence: read_json_auto auto-inference is convenient but can misidentify types. Schema declaration would be more deterministic.
current_substrate_inventory.adjacent_tool_potential: DuckDB already handles JSONL→Parquet well. Explicit schema declaration (vs read_json_auto inference) would improve reliability. PyArrow could provide schema-first Parquet writes.

current_substrate_inventory.current_role: Session lifecycle finalize — compacts JSONL to .jsonl.gz, manages storage budgets, produces lifecycle receipts
current_substrate_inventory.source_of_truth_status: derived artifact — canonical JSONL files are preserved; gzip is cold storage
current_substrate_inventory.performance_constraints: gzip compression is moderate speed, moderate ratio. Line-by-line JSONL read + gzip write per session.
current_substrate_inventory.bottleneck_evidence: gzip is adequate for session-level compaction. zstandard (already a dependency) would provide better compression ratio and speed for archive bundles — but is currently unused for this purpose.
current_substrate_inventory.adjacent_tool_potential: Zstandard is already a canonical dependency but only used for teleport diff compression. Expanding to session/bundle/archive compression is low-risk and high-reward.

current_substrate_inventory.current_role: Streaming LLM response client — parses SSE data chunks with json.loads per chunk
current_substrate_inventory.source_of_truth_status: runtime-only — raw responses are never persisted
current_substrate_inventory.performance_constraints: json.loads(data_str) per SSE chunk — inherent to OpenAI-compatible streaming protocol. 10s-100s of chunks per request. Not a bottleneck.
current_substrate_inventory.bottleneck_evidence: SSE chunk parsing is frequent but lightweight (<1KB JSON per chunk). No optimization needed.
current_substrate_inventory.adjacent_tool_potential: orjson could accelerate json.loads for SSE chunks but the benefit is marginal (<5% of total request latency). Not worth the dependency cost.

current_substrate_inventory.current_role: Context assembly pipeline — builds symbol indexes, repo maps, active work lane summaries for LLM context
current_substrate_inventory.source_of_truth_status: derived runtime artifact — context packets are per-session computed
current_substrate_inventory.performance_constraints: Symbol extraction via tree-sitter is the bottleneck. Context assembly is CPU-bound, not I/O-bound.
current_substrate_inventory.bottleneck_evidence: Tree-sitter parsing dominates context assembly latency. No JSONL/Parquet/Arrow benefit — this is a compute problem.
current_substrate_inventory.adjacent_tool_potential: pgvector could accelerate similar-failure/remediation-plan semantic lookup from content-light report corpus — but this is retrieval, not assembly.

existing_adjacent_dependencies.status: actively used for JSONL→in-memory analytical views and JSONL→Parquet compaction. Dominates analytical read-side need.
canonical dependency but only used for teleport diff compression. Underutilized — should expand to session bundles, archive compaction, and export packages.
core model layer. model_dump_json() used for serialization. Type-safe boundary between JSON artifacts and Python objects.
canonical schema validation. Used by static docs renderer and telemetry bundle validator. Should remain the primary boundary validation — database-side validation is defense-in-depth.

static docs template rendering. No high-performance concern — batch offline renderer.
